column3: Agent Client Protocol — Overview. agentclientprotocol.com, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: Anthropic's ACP is a client-to-agent (editor-to-agent) protocol using JSON-RPC 2.0; it is not an agent-to-agent orchestration protocol and has no Go SDK.
column6: Primary source. Documented methods (initialize/authenticate/session.*/fs.*/terminal.*) confirm client-to-agent scope.

column4: A2A is JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP(S) with sync/SSE streaming/async push; core concepts are Agent Cards (optionally signed) Tasks Messages and Skills; IBM's ACP was incorporated into A2A; A2A is positioned as complementary to MCP.
column6: Primary source from the official A2A documentation site.

column3: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) Repository README. github.com/a2aproject/A2A, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: A2A v1.0.0 released 2026-03-12 with official SDKs for Python Go JS Java and .NET; authorization scheme embedded in AgentCard is on the roadmap.
column6: Primary source. Confirms Go SDK availability at github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go.

column3: A2A Protocol and its Relationship to MCP. a2a-protocol.org/latest/, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: A2A is described as the 'public internet' allowing agents including those using MCP to interoperate; Cisco's agntcy framework leverages both.
column6: Direct quote from the official A2A homepage; confirms complementary positioning.

column3: Linux Foundation: Linux Foundation Launches the Agent2Agent Protocol Project. linuxfoundation.org/press/, June 2025.
column4: Linux Foundation formed the A2A project with AWS Cisco Google Microsoft Salesforce SAP and ServiceNow at Open Source Summit North America 2025.
column6: Authoritative press release confirming governance transfer.

column4: A2A v1.0 turns the spec into production-grade with Signed Agent Cards; AP2 ships as a formal extension.
column6: Release tag confirms v1.0 date and Signed Agent Cards as a v1 feature.

column4: IBM ACP merged with A2A under the Linux Foundation AI and Data umbrella in August 2025; BeeAI platform now uses A2A.

column4: LangGraph multi-agent handoffs use Command objects returned from handoff tools; MCP integration is supported for tool communication; no native A2A support is documented inside LangGraph itself.
column6: Primary source for LangGraph's own model; A2A bridging happens at process boundaries and is out of LangGraph's scope.

column3: MCP vs A2A vs ACP — AI Agent Protocols Compared. bonjoy.com/articles/mcp-vs-a2a-vs-acp-agent-protocols-compared/, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: MCP connects agents to tools; A2A connects agents to agents; ACP (Anthropic) connects agents to editors — three complementary protocols solving different layers.
column6: Secondary analysis but matches primary-source positioning; used for positioning confirmation not primary claims.
